title: Basic
summary: Four isolates on three event loops: A and B on workers of their own, C and D sharing a pool. Each has a Block and a Crash button, so you can see what a failure takes down and what keeps running. The landing page runs it live, as the recording.

shows.text: Containment: a blocked loop stalls only what shares it
Pools: C and D share a worker, so they stall and restart together
Restarts, and a member's own error restarting it alone
The crash-loop guard: three crashes within a minute and the kernel stops

try: Block C for 3 s: D stalls with it, since they share a worker, and after 2 s both restart. A and B keep counting.
Crash D: only D restarts, even in the pool, because it reports the error as its own.
Crash A three times within a minute: the kernel stops restarting it, and its pane offers Restart A. B, C and D carry on.
Block the main thread: every surface freezes on screen while the loops behind them keep running.

measurements.note: No measurements: Basic is for watching containment and restarts, not for measuring their cost. The dashboards measure that.
